text:
Predicates:
Managed(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Deposit(x, y) ::: a deposit of x is required to rent an apartment in y.
Rent(x, y) ::: the monthly rent at x is y.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: the security deposit at x is y.
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed in y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Owns(x, y) ::: x owns y.
Premises:
∃x (Managed(x) ∧ Allowed(pets, x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (Managed(x) → ∃y Deposit(y, x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (Managed(x) → ∀y (SecurityDeposit(y, x) → (y = Rent(y, x) ∨ y > Rent(y, x)))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to the monthly rent at a managed building or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
Managed(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(2000, oliveGarden) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
2000 > 1500 ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
(∃x (Managed(x) ∧ Allowed(fluffy, x) ∧ SecurityDeposit(≤1500, x)) → Rents(tom, x)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
∀x (Managed(x) → (Allowed(pets, x) → ∀y (Pet(y) → Allowed(y, x)))) ::: If a managed building allows pets, then people are allowed to move in with a pet.
Conclusion:
Allowed(fluffy, oliveGarden) ::: Tom is allowed to move into an apartment in The Olive Garden with Fluffy.
